title: Example 19-2: Morse Code (Letters Added for Readability)

illustrates.quote: b. Insert a blank cell between individual symbols for a word. c. Insert three blank cells between words.

blocks.features: Verified against the PDF page image (p.520): the letters M-O-R-S-E and C-O-D-E are printed above their own Morse dot/dash sequence, spaced out to align each letter over its own code; there is a wide gap between the two words. Not print text a transcriber would normally include (the title itself says "Letters Added for Readability") — Emboss has no column-alignment mechanism for this in any case (F-219).

print.notes: The print shows the letters of MORSE CODE spaced out with their own Morse code symbols aligned directly beneath each letter; per the example's own title, the letters are an add-on aid, not something a real transcription would carry (the braille below omits them entirely, per 19.4.1's own instruction to show only the symbols).

braille.notes: Byte-identical between run A and run B, and independently re-derived from source-line 15084 (fixed 9-space Example margin stripped, U+2800→space, which is what preserves the three-cell gap between the two Morse words per 19.4.1c).

resolution: Braille unchanged (A and B agree, byte-identical, confirmed by independent re-extraction). Print side: the letters and their own alignment are decorative (per the example's own title) and not braille-buildable in this schema regardless (F-219/F-222); kept as a documented 'other' limitation rather than modeled, matching both runs' own intent.
